title: Duck / Rotating module explainer

chapters.title: Hear the world
bullets: A host links sensing and motion
sentences: Meet Duck: four microphones, a camera, and a moving body. Let us rotate and open it up.

chapters.title: Lid & acoustic interface
sentences: The lid aligns four sound entries with the microphones. Its contact lands meet the acoustic pads; bayonet features locate and retain the cover.

chapters.title: Head enclosure
bullets: Space for host, optics and wiring
Blue rim with a black front band
sentences: The shell supports the lid and microphone board, while packaging the computer, optics and wiring. Its blue rim and black front band stay together.

chapters.title: Four microphone array
sentences: Four microphones sample the sound field. The audio processor combines their signals, providing processed audio and inputs for sound direction and voice activity.

chapters.title: XIAO audio bridge
sentences: Radxa connects to XIAO by USB for audio and control. This firmware carries sixteen kilohertz stereo audio: two processed channels from four microphones.
chapters.note: XIAO is on the circular board. Cable geometry is a packaging reference.

chapters.title: Main computer
sentences: The Radxa computer runs Linux applications. It receives audio and visual input, then coordinates interaction through the robot interface.

chapters.title: Robot interface board
sentences: The robot interface board links the host, servos and power. Its six axis sensor measures acceleration and angular velocity for body motion awareness.
chapters.note: The IMU belongs to this board; individual IC geometry is not modelled.

chapters.title: Camera & optics
sentences: The lens, holder and front panel position the optical assembly. Images reach the host, where applications can combine vision with hearing.
chapters.note: Source optical assembly; no unconfirmed image sensor model is implied.

chapters.title: Speaker
sentences: The speaker turns audio signals into sound. This source model shows its installation envelope; the output circuit must match the actual wiring.
chapters.note: The grey block is the original speaker envelope, not a detailed speaker model.

chapters.title: Beak & head mechanism
sentences: The beak combines upper and lower parts with soft contact pieces. Brackets and bearings support the mechanism; this open pose illustrates its structure.
chapters.note: Display articulation; actuation and collision clearance are not validated.

chapters.title: Battery & power
sentences: The rear battery supplies the robot through its power circuitry. Support parts retain the pack. The model does not establish capacity or runtime.
chapters.note: NP-F battery envelope; capacity and runtime are not inferred.

chapters.title: Fifteen smart servos
sentences: Fifteen smart servos move the head, neck and legs. Bus commands set targets; each servo runs local control and returns status.

chapters.title: Frame, legs & feet
sentences: The frame connects the body and limbs. Bearings support joints, while feet and soft soles contact the ground. Walking requires separate control software.

chapters.title: Firmware & host tools
sentences: Firmware handles USB audio and device controls. Host tools display signals and voice activity events. Application hooks support further integration.
chapters.note: Voice activity is not keyword recognition. Assistant services are separate.

chapters.title: Back to one robot
sentences: The modules return while Duck keeps turning: sensing, computing and interaction, with matching model sources, firmware and host code.

notes: Rigid exploded illustration, not a validated physical removal sequence.
Current firmware requires Radxa USB HOST to XIAO USB; the imported cable mesh is only an older packaging reference.
Board-level geometry is retained as supplied. Unmodelled individual ICs are described without invented geometry.
Speaker routing, physical assembly, acoustics and robot control require hardware verification.
English narration is synthesized locally, not a real microphone recording.
